messages:
Maya (Customer Ops): kickoff — running tabletop drill for incident communications. Scenario: embeddings service degraded for a subset of customers. This is a dry run; no real customers affected. Goal: practice status page + customer notification + on-call handoff language. Please use real comms tone.

Incident Bot: :rotating_light: This is a scheduled drill triggered by @Maya. Drill ID: DRL-2026-03-15-01. No real paging will be sent.

Sasha (oncall): on it — taking incident lead for the drill. I’ll simulate detection -> triage -> mitigation steps.

Raj (DevOps): noted. I’ll stand by for mitigation commands and will mock the infra actions. Also adding a quick checklist of what we’d run:
```
- check cluster health: rgi status embeddings-cluster
- validate GPU pool: rgi pool list --name embeddings
- inspect recent deploys: rgi deploys --since 2h --service embeddings
- tail logs: rgi logs embeddings --filter error --lines 200
```

Emily (Product): for the status page we should be clear about scope and ETA. Drafting candidate content for the public status page below. Please comment on tone/accuracy.

Emily (Product): [STATUS PAGE DRAFT]
"Service: Embeddings — Degraded"
"Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency or timeouts for embedding creation. Not all customers affected; we're investigating routing and autoscaling behavior."
"Current status: Identifying root cause and applying mitigations. Estimated next update: in 15 minutes."
"What we're doing: Our on-call team is investigating routing and GPU availability. We'll update with impact scope and mitigations as we confirm them."

Maya (Customer Ops): good start. For customers with SLOs, we should include a proactive notification template they can send to their stakeholders. Drafting short customer email: 

"Subject: Temporary Degradation in Embeddings API — We're on it"
"Hi <CustomerName>,
We wanted to let you know we are investigating a temporary degradation in our Embeddings API that may cause slower responses for some requests. Our engineering team is actively mitigating the issue and we will provide updates via our status page (status.redwood.com). No action is required from your side at this time. We expect to have an initial update within 15 minutes.
Thanks,
Redwood Customer Ops"

Sasha (oncall): adding an internal handoff template for when we escalate to next-shift if needed: 
"Handoff (to next on-call):
Root cause so far: suspected routing/batch queue stall affecting embeddings nodes.
Actions taken: restarted pool embeddings-v2 (mock), scaled replicas +2, applied temporary bypass for legacy model.
Open tasks: correlate with recent quantization rollout, validate KV cache integrity.
Next steps: follow up on logs and run additional canary tests.
"

Frank (Eng SRE): nit: call out exact metrics in the status page so customers can triage: e.g., 95th pct latency for embedding-create increased to ~1.2s from 200ms, error rate at 0.6% for affected zone. Keep ETA conservative.

Emily (Product): updated status draft with metrics and clearer ETA. New draft: 

[STATUS PAGE DRAFT v2]
Service: Embeddings — Degraded
Impact: Increased latency and intermittent errors for embedding creation for a subset of customers in us-west-2.
Current metrics: p95 latency ~1.2s (baseline ~200ms), errors ~0.6% of calls in affected zone.
Scope: ~7% of requests routed via embeddings-v2 pool.
Estimated next update: 15 minutes.
What we're doing: Scaling embedding pool, investigating recent model rollout and routing layer; on-call performing targeted restarts on affected nodes.

Maya (Customer Ops): love that. For the customer email template, add a short workaround note for power users: "If you need immediate embeddings, try limiting batch size to 1 or route to the fallback embeddings model by adding model=fallback-embed to your request."

Sasha (oncall): mocked mitigation: applied scale +2 and rolled back a small routing change (simulated command below).
```
# simulated commands for drill
rgi pool scale embeddings-v2 --replicas +2 --reason "drill mitigation"
rgi route update embeddings --policy revert --change-id CHG-1234
```

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Drill action recorded. Mitigation simulated by @Sasha. Drill log: DRL-2026-03-15-01.

Maya (Customer Ops): next, let's run the internal brief to execs template — short one-pager we give to PM/Eng leaders. Draft: 
"Summary: Temporary degradation in Embeddings API observed in us-west-2. Customer impact: increased latency and small error rate affecting approx 7% of traffic. Mitigation: scaled pool and reverted routing change; investigating possible correlation with recent quantization rollout. No customer-facing data loss.
Current ETA: next update in 15 mins.
Owner: Sasha (oncall).
Ask: Engineering to validate root cause and confirm rollback; product to prepare status text; customer ops to send proactive email to affected customers if error rate persists >1% for 15 minutes"

Frank (Eng SRE): feedback on exec note: add risk/blast radius and whether Dedicated customers are impacted differently. Also include whether any contractual SLAs might be triggered.

Emily (Product): incorporated Frank's feedback. Updated exec note ready.

Sasha (oncall): thumbs up. For the drill wrap, let's run a quick retrospective checklist in thread:
- Did status page copy clearly state scope? :white_check_mark:
- Did customer email indicate expected ETA? :white_check_mark:
- Was internal handoff template sufficiently actionable? :thinking:
- Were mitigation steps reproducible in runbook? :white_check_mark:

Maya (Customer Ops): action item: I'll collect feedback and produce final templates in the incident-comm-templates folder after the drill. Also scheduling a 30-min follow-up to practice the actual send cadence.

Raj (DevOps): note for runbooks: we should add a quick run that verifies KV cache warmup after restarts — saved us time last time.

Frank (Eng SRE): one more thought — include a short blameless language checklist for customer replies, e.g., "We're actively investigating and will keep you updated" vs. "We caused an outage". Keeps tone neutral and helpful.

Maya (Customer Ops): good point. Will standardize language.

Sasha (oncall): wrap — thanks all. Drill complete. Recording: https://zoom.mock/drill/DRL-2026-03-15-01 (mock). Please add any leftover comments here and I'll follow up with runbook edits + a versioned status page draft.

Emily (Product): small follow-up: can someone own publishing the status page if we validate mitigation? I can prepare the copy but need someone with publish perms.

Raj (DevOps): I can publish in drill scenarios. Tag me when ready.

Maya (Customer Ops): thanks team — great practice. Posting retrospective action items in #incidents-retros soon. :sparkles:
